messages:
Oncall Bot: [PAGER] Severity: P1 — inference-latency-us-west - high p95/p99 observed, alerting threshold breached (p99 > 2.5s)

Alex R.: paging — I'm on it. seeing sustained p95 ~1.8s and p99 ~3.1s for text-gen (gpt-3-like) on us-west-1 dedicated pool. errors low but tail latency high.

Maria Chen: noted. is this all models or specific model variant? any recent deploys?

Alex R.: only heavy for model: redwood/gptx-7b-ct2-quant on the dedicated GPU pool. no deploys in last 2 hrs. autoscaler didn't add nodes last spike.

Jamal K.: looking at allocator logs now. possible queueing in the runtime. dumping top-of-queue and kernel metrics.

Katy Lee: customers_reporting = 2 during last 10m via support queue. both reported slow responses but no 5xx. adding to incident notes.

Alex R.: runbook step 1: check routing + overload protections. run: `redwoodctl routes inspect --pool us-west-1 --model gptx-7b-ct2-quant`

Alex R.: output snippet: ```
route: us-west-1/gptx-7b-ct2-quant
active_replicas: 8
queued_requests: 420
avg_serving_tokens_per_sec: 3200
cpu/gpu_util: gpu 94%
```

Maria Chen: GPU at 94% — KV cache thrash maybe. try enabling prefix caching and reduce max_tokens for live traffic as hotfix. we can also temporarily route small requests to a cheaper variant.

Jamal K.: attempting targeted scale up: `redwoodctl pool scale --pool us-west-1 --min 12 --burst 16` — requesting extra capacity. triggering allocation.

Oncall Bot: Autoscaler event: allocation_request(submitted) id=alloc-98765. ETA provisioning ~6-9 minutes per infra.

Katy Lee: drafting status page update (short & customer-facing):
"Status: Degraded performance in US-WEST inference pool affecting text generation latency. We are actively mitigating and have initiated capacity scale-up. Some requests may experience slower response times; no errors or data loss observed. Next update in 15 minutes or as status changes."

Priya Nair: suggested customer email (for affected accounts):
Subject: Brief service slowdown affecting inference latency (US-West)
Body:
Hi — We’re experiencing a temporary slowdown in inference response times for models served from our US-West pool. Our engineers are actively scaling capacity and applying mitigations. We expect recovery within ~30–60 minutes. We’ll follow up when normal performance is restored. Apologies for the disruption. — Redwood Inference Status

Alex R.: mitigation checklist I'm executing now:
- escalate autoscale (done)
- re-route small/non-critical traffic to us-east fallback (planning)
- lower `max_tokens` per request via temporary policy:
```
policy set: rate_limit_small_requests: 512 tokens
policy target: pool us-west-1
```
- apply runtime restart on the worst nodes if provisioning slow

Jamal K.: provisioning progressing. node bootstrap logs show container image pull delay on one host (registry throttling). starting warm-start on reserved nodes to speed up.

Oncall Bot: Incident note added by Alex R.: "Attempted autoscale, enabled throttles, preparing fallback routing."

Maria Chen: small impact plan: add a routing rule to send requests with prompt_length < 200 tokens to cheaper `gptx-3.5-slim` variant in us-west until capacity stabilizes. Command: `redwoodctl routing patch --pool us-west-1 --rule 'if prompt_len<200 then model=gptx-3.5-slim'`

Katy Lee: support template for copy/paste into support threads:
"We are currently observing higher-than-normal latency for text generation in US-West. Our engineering team is actively applying mitigations including scaling and routing changes. We estimate normal performance to return within 30–60 minutes. We'll update you as soon as we have more info. — Redwood Support"

Alex R.: applying the routing patch now.

Support Bot: Notice queued to affected customers list id=notif-5532. ETA send ~2 min.

Jamal K.: rolling restart on 3 nodes to clear suspected KV cache fragmentation: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime -n redwood --selector zone=us-west-1 --max-unavailable=1`

Maria Chen: observe after restart if p99 drops — restart should be safe (low error rate).

Alex R.: p95 down to 1.1s after first 3 new nodes came up and routing rule applied. p99 down to ~1.9s. queued_requests now 120. good trend.

Katy Lee: updating status page to include ETA: "Next update in 20 minutes. Estimated recovery: partial recovery within 30 minutes, full recovery as autoscaling completes (~60 minutes)."

Priya Nair: final customer-facing note pre-send: "We implemented temporary routing and capacity increases. Latency is improving, and we will monitor closely. No action required from your side. Reach out if you continue to see impact."

Alex R.: summary for handoff -> next on-call (in 15m):
- incident: high tail latency in us-west dedicated pool; cause: capacity saturation + registry pull delays slowed autoscale.
- mitigations applied: autoscale request, routing rule for small requests, rolling restarts on 3 nodes, temporary token caps.
- current status: improving (p99 ~1.6s, p95 ~0.9s), queued_requests 60, provisioning still +2 nodes pending.
- follow-ups: watch registry pull errors, ensure autoscaler converges to min=12, confirm no regression after routing rollback.

Oncall Bot: Handoff reminder: @Maria Chen will take next shift in 15 minutes. Please add any open tasks to the incident thread.

Maria Chen: taking handoff. noted action items. will watch for churn after routing rollback and coordinate rollback plan if necessary.

Alex R.: sending final internal update to #eng-oncall and #product for visibility. thx team. :thumbsup:

Support Bot: Customers notified: 2 affected accounts, email dispatched. Incident ticket updated.

Oncall Bot: Incident closed? Not yet — monitoring for stability for next 45 minutes.

Alex R.: marking incident as "mitigated" in our tracker; leaving thread open for post-incident notes and RCA prep.

"""
